This probabilistic forecast is then used to compute expected financial cost F_cost = P_injury × L_loss, where L_loss represents average injury-induced revenue loss. The second operator 'financial_impact_quantification' formalizes this linkage by modeling C_fin = Σ_i P_injury(i) × L_loss(i), assuming independence across players. Failure modes include overfitting due to small sample sizes or misclassification of rare events, and leakage from unobserved confounders such as medical history or environmental factors. Dualities emerge between workload accumulation and recovery dynamics, suggesting that optimal rest scheduling minimizes both injury risk and associated financial loss.
